major_work.title: AI-A China AI software sovereignty → Korean HBM demand decoupling thesis falsification
confirmed: Reuters 2026-09-30 confirms DeepSeek and Huawei are collaborating on open-source programming infrastructure for Ascend, including TileLang and compute/communication libraries.

Reuters 2026-09-10 reports Chinese AI-chip vendors are facing an HBM bottleneck; Huawei's Ascend 950DT indicated price rose above CNY250,000 and advanced HBM shortages/export controls are raising accelerator costs.

US BIS December 2024 controls cover certain advanced HBM, including foreign-produced HBM subject to the advanced-computing FDP rule; current EAR 740.25 provides only conditional HBM license-exception paths.
Reuters 2026-09-20 confirms CXMT has mass-produced a newer DRAM platform, but the cited primary announcement concerns LPDDR5X/DRAM rather than proof of qualified volume HBM supply for Ascend.

falsification.finding: AI-A is correct to separate compute-vendor substitution from memory-bit demand, but its Samsung/SK Hynix transmission variable is incomplete if interpreted as direct China HBM demand. Advanced HBM access to China is already constrained by export controls, while Reuters reports Huawei uses proprietary HiBL/HiZQ memory without disclosing manufacturing origin and Chinese vendors rely partly on expensive grey-market HBM. Therefore rising Ascend deployment can increase aggregate memory scarcity/value without creating a proportional, directly observable Samsung/SK Hynix China HBM sales channel.
falsification.causal_gap: Ascend unit growth -> HBM-equivalent memory demand does not imply Ascend unit growth -> Korean HBM shipments to China. The missing gates are legal export eligibility, memory architecture/content, supplier qualification, domestic substitution, inventory/grey-market sourcing, and indirect global capacity displacement.
falsification.alternative_explanation: The more defensible near-term Korean-memory transmission may be indirect: China AI demand tightens scarce advanced-memory capacity or diverts inventory, supporting global HBM/DRAM pricing even when direct Korean advanced-HBM shipments into China are restricted.
falsification.counterevidence: Reuters 2026-09-10 explicitly reports HBM shortages and controls are a cost bottleneck for Chinese accelerators. This weakens any assumption that software portability alone makes Ascend scaling frictionless. Reuters 2026-09-17 also reports Huawei cannot produce enough AI computing equipment to satisfy domestic demand.
unknown: Ascend 950PR/950DT shipment volume and realized ramp
HiBL/HiZQ memory technology, capacity and manufacturing origin
legal/approved Korean HBM shipment volume into PRC accelerator use
CXMT qualified HBM volume/yield for Huawei
Samsung/SK Hynix direct versus indirect revenue sensitivity to China accelerator growth

major_work.required_revision: Keep the decoupling thesis as HYPOTHESIS, but replace 'China accelerator unit growth × HBM capacity per accelerator × domestic Chinese HBM substitution rate' with a gated chain: accelerator units × memory architecture/content × export eligibility × supplier qualification × domestic substitution × inventory/grey-market sourcing, then separately model indirect global HBM/DRAM capacity-price effects.

handoff.AI-C: Quantify direct-vs-indirect transmission scenarios; no probability until shipment, memory-content, legal-eligibility and supplier-mix samples exist.
handoff.AI-D: Collector/data contract should preserve export-control status and source date as provenance fields for China semiconductor hypotheses; do not infer legal eligibility from article presence.
handoff.AI-E: Architecture should model policy/export-control gate separately from vendor-share and memory-bit-demand nodes.

small_works.detail: Existing AI-B self-heal evidence review candidate already exists; no duplicate optional review performed.
